narration.text: A standoff annotation can describe a range of text. But it can also connect that text to something beyond the document.

caption: A textual occurrence is not an entity.

narration.text: The word Napoleon is a textual occurrence. The person it refers to is an independently identifiable entity.
A mention annotation records the association between a particular range of text and the entity to which it refers.

caption: A bridge between text and knowledge.

narration.text: When that association is represented in a database, the annotation becomes a bridge between the textual world and the world of structured knowledge.
Across many documents, different words and expressions can refer to the same entity.
Each occurrence has its own context, and each mention has its own identity.
Conversely, the same expression can refer to different entities.
It is the recorded association, not the wording alone, that identifies the referent.

caption: From text to knowledge. From knowledge to text.

narration.text: These connections can be followed in either direction: from a textual occurrence to its entity, or from an entity to the passages in which it is mentioned.

caption: Text need not become a graph. It can be connected to one.

narration.text: Text need not become a graph.
It can be connected to one.
